title: Idolatrous Elders and Inevitable Judgment

questions.question: When some of the elders of Israel came to Ezekiel and sat before him, what did the Lord say these men had done?
options: Taken their idols into their hearts and set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces
Broken the covenant of the Sabbath openly in the streets
Conspired to assassinate the king of Babylon
Sold their daughters into slavery
questions.correctAnswer: Taken their idols into their hearts and set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:3 (ESV): "Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts, and set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. Should I indeed let myself be consulted by them?"

questions.question: How will the Lord answer anyone of the house of Israel who takes his idols into his heart and comes to the prophet?
options: He will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols
He will strike him with leprosy
He will answer him with fire from heaven
He will refuse to answer him entirely
questions.correctAnswer: He will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:4 (ESV): "I the Lord will answer him as he comes with the multitude of his idols,"

questions.question: Why does the Lord say He will do this to them?
options: That I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who are all estranged from me through their idols
To show the nations that the prophets are worthless
So that they may be shamed in the presence of Babylon
To make them wealthy through divination
questions.correctAnswer: That I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who are all estranged from me through their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:5 (ESV): "that I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who are all estranged from me through their idols."

questions.question: What is God's command to the house of Israel through Ezekiel?
options: "Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations."
"Sacrifice an unblemished lamb for your sins."
"Fast for forty days and wear sackcloth."
"Take up the sword and defend the temple."
questions.correctAnswer: "Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:6 (ESV): "Therefore say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord God: Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations."

questions.question: What will God make the person who turns away from Him to set up idols, yet comes to the prophet?
options: A sign and a byword, and cut him off from the midst of my people
A laughingstock in the streets of Jerusalem
A slave to the Chaldeans forever
A monument of stone
questions.correctAnswer: A sign and a byword, and cut him off from the midst of my people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:8 (ESV): "And I will set my face against that man; I will make him a sign and a byword and cut him off from the midst of my people..."

questions.question: If a prophet is deceived and speaks a word in such a case, who has deceived that prophet?
options: I, the Lord, have deceived that prophet
The evil spirit of Baal
His own greedy heart
The kings of the nations
questions.correctAnswer: I, the Lord, have deceived that prophet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:9 (ESV): "And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the Lord, have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him..."

questions.question: What will be the punishment of both the inquirer and the prophet?
options: The punishment of the prophet and the punishment of the inquirer shall be alike
The prophet will be stoned, but the inquirer exiled
The prophet will lose his voice, and the inquirer his wealth
The inquirer will be forgiven, but the prophet killed
questions.correctAnswer: The punishment of the prophet and the punishment of the inquirer shall be alike
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:10 (ESV): "And they shall bear their punishment—the punishment of the prophet and the punishment of the inquirer shall be alike—"

questions.question: What does God say He will stretch out against a land that sins against Him by acting faithlessly, to break its supply of bread?
options: His hand to send famine
The sword of Babylon
A swarm of locusts
A great fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:13 (ESV): "...and I stretch out my hand against it and break its supply of bread and send famine upon it, and cut off from it man and beast,"

questions.question: Which three righteous men does God name, saying that even if they were in the land, they could only deliver their own lives by their righteousness?
options: Noah, Daniel, and Job
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Moses, Samuel, and David
Elijah, Elisha, and Isaiah
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14 (ESV): "even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord God."

questions.question: If God brings wild beasts through the land to bereave it, what could these three faithful men deliver?
options: Only themselves; they could not deliver sons or daughters
The whole city
Their wives and children only
The livestock of the land
questions.correctAnswer: Only themselves; they could not deliver sons or daughters
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:16 (ESV): "even if these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord God, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be delivered, but the land would be desolate."

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four disastrous acts of judgment God promises to send upon Jerusalem?
options: Earthquake
Sword
Famine
Wild beasts
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:21 (ESV): "How much more when I send upon Jerusalem my four disastrous acts of judgment, sword, famine, wild beasts, and pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast!"

questions.question: What is the fourth disastrous act of judgment listed in verse 21?
options: Pestilence
Floods
Fire from heaven
Hailstones
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:21 (ESV): "...sword, famine, wild beasts, and pestilence..."

questions.question: What will happen when a remnant (sons and daughters) is brought out of Jerusalem and comes to Ezekiel and the exiles?
options: "You will see their ways and their deeds, and you will be consoled for the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem."
"They will sing songs of deliverance."
"They will bring great treasures from the temple."
"You will reject them as unclean."
questions.correctAnswer: "You will see their ways and their deeds, and you will be consoled for the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:22 (ESV): "you will see their ways and their deeds, and you will be consoled for the disaster that I have brought upon Jerusalem,"

questions.question: Why will Ezekiel and the exiles be consoled when they see the ways of the remnant that was judged?
options: Because they will know that God had not done without cause all that He had done in it
Because they will be reunited with their families
Because the remnant will bring messages of peace
Because God will promise an immediate return
questions.correctAnswer: Because they will know that God had not done without cause all that He had done in it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:23 (ESV): "They will console you, when you see their ways and their deeds, and you shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, declares the Lord God."

questions.question: Through what primary means did the people estrange themselves from the Lord, according to verses 4 and 5?
options: Through their idols
Through making alliances with Egypt
Through fighting the Babylonians
Through intermarrying with the Canaanites
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:5 (ESV): "that I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, who are all estranged from me through their idols."

key_verse_text: "even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord God."
